chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Durays ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who permits his brother to have intercourse with his slave-girl while she goes out for his needs,

He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is permissible for him.' I asked: 'What do you think if she bears a child, what is done with him?' He said: 'He belongs to the master of the slave-girl, unless he stipulated for her when he permitted her that if she bears a child, he is free.' He said: 'If he did so, he is free.' I asked: 'Does he own his child?' He said: 'If he has wealth, he buys him at the price.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child born from a slave-girl permitted to another man?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the fiqh of *Ihlal* (permitting a slave-girl for another), specifically addressing the paternity and manumission status of offspring born from such unions. It establishes the default rule that the child belongs to the master, unless a prior condition of freedom (*itq*) was explicitly stipulated, in which case the master must purchase the child's freedom at market value if he retains ownership. This ruling highlights the interplay between contractual stipulations and the inherent rights of slaves in Shia jurisprudence.
